categories: AI & Automation, Banking & Payments, Practice Management
description: For larger businesses, the gap between 'getting the data in' and 'getting the money out' is where profitability dies for an accounting firm. Join FreeAgent and Apron as we reveal how the implementation of a number of AI tools bridges this gap. Learn how to build a tech stack that thinks for itself - identifying patterns, managing complex workflows, and executing payments with superhuman accuracy. This isn't just about saving time, it's about using the tech ecosystem to offer a premium service that scales without increasing your headcount.

title: Taming the mess with bespoke AI
description: The real world is messy. For thousands of years, accountants have been there to tame that mess. Just as computers led to an explosion in the volume and complexity of data and insights that were achievable, AI now promises to do the same. But AI is so much more than ChatGPT and Large Language Models. Grant Thornton UK's research lab has designed their own AI architecture for accounting data, accessing unprecedented levels of depth and relational richness inside the debits and credits. This session introduces the lab and presents their AI's spooky ability to find missing transactions in a general ledger.

title: How accountants are getting real value from AI
description: Artificial intelligence promises to transform the accounting industry, but separating genuine value from hype can be challenging. In this session, Bright's AI expert Euan Matthews shows how accountants can leverage AI to deliver real value for their practice, including improving efficiency, analysing client data to identify trends and opportunities, and creating new service lines for clients. Attendees will gain practical techniques they can apply in daily workflows to protect data, enhance margins, deliver better client outcomes, and differentiate their practice in a competitive market.

title: Technology, ethics and accountability: What modern accountancy demands
description: Technology is changing how you work, but it does not change your ethical responsibilities. As new systems and AI-enabled tools become part of everyday practice, ethical codes now place greater emphasis on how technology is selected, used and overseen. This session explains what those changes mean in practice. Using real-world scenarios, Julia explores situations where technology can unintentionally compromise ethical standards, and sets out practical steps you can take to manage risk, maintain accountability and avoid ethical breaches.

title: The intersection of the human/AI paradigm
categories: AI, AI & Automation, Data & Analytics, HR & People, Practice Management
description: This session explores how accountants can integrate AI into their workflows while keeping people at the center. The panel will discuss how AI supports accuracy, efficiency and deeper insight, and how professionals can evolve their skills without losing the human judgment, empathy and trust that clients rely on. By the end of the session, participants will have a toolkit of prompting techniques they can immediately apply to make AI work smarter for them.

title: AI doesn't fit today's accounting systems: Why real automation needs a new foundation
description: AI is often talked about as a smarter add-on to existing accounting software. In reality, it changes the rules entirely. This session explains why meaningful automation can't be achieved by simply layering AI onto today's accounting systems, and what a new foundation needs to look like. Attendees will gain a clear mental model for how AI is reshaping accounting, why month-end exists at all, and what this shift means for firms planning their future.

title: Neurodivergent leadership: The high-performance edge and the hidden cost of mental health
categories: Neurodiversity, Tax & MTD, HR & People, Marketing & Growth, Practice Management
description: Many firm owners and their teams are white-knuckling it, masking struggles just to survive the day. We talk tax and tech, but ignore the neurodivergent (ND) brain—the engine that drives success but can lead to burnout, isolation, or addiction. I'm pulling back the curtain on the ND reality in our profession. We'll explore the tactical edge of the 'different' brain, the traps of high-pressure leadership, and how to build a team where ND talent thrives. No clinical fluff—just a raw look at staying sane while scaling, and how to harness the unique abilities of your team while protecting them from the ND risks they face.

title: It's 2026, but your Excel skills are in 1993

Yet, most finance professionals are still talking about VLOOKUP and PivotTables; the features that have long since been surpassed. The problem isn't Excel; the problem is your skills are so outdated that you don't know these modern features even exist.

title: Beyond the numbers: Building leadership capability in accountancy firms
categories: Engagement / Recruitment / Training / Development / Upskilling / Retention / HR, HR & People
description: The accountancy profession excels at technical training but consistently under invests in leadership development. description: Family Investment Companies (FICs) are increasingly used to preserve and pass on wealth while retaining control. This seminar will take a practical look at how FICs can hold property, trading businesses and investment portfolios, enabling the older generation to control strategy and income while passing value to future generations. It will cover structuring, governance and common pitfalls, and show how FICs can be tax efficient for IHT, CGT and Income Tax. A must-attend session for accountants and tax advisers to family and entrepreneurial clients.

title: UK GAAP after the periodic review: Practical implications for year one
description: The 2024 Periodic Review of UK GAAP brings a range of changes that will affect how entities recognise transactions, draft accounting policies and explain their results. While revenue recognition and lease accounting are areas of focus, changes include increasing the level of judgement, documentation and disclosure required across the financial statements. This session takes a practical look at how to prepare for the first set of financial statements under the revised standards, helping preparers and auditors understand priorities, where challenges are likely to arise and how to approach transition with confidence.

title: Salary vs. dividends: Top 5 profit extraction strategies
categories: Tax / VAT / MTD, Tax & MTD, Data & Analytics
description: From 2025/26, directors of close companies must itemise dividends on tax returns, giving HMRC clearer insight into total remuneration. With rising taxes and closer scrutiny, profit extraction is becoming more challenging. This seminar explores whether the salary–dividend model still works, HMRC's view on acceptable planning, the impact of recent income tax and NI changes, and practical alternative strategies, pitfalls and guidance for advisers supporting directors.

title: FRS 102 leases: Your 2026 implementation toolkit
categories: Regulation & Legislation, Data & Analytics, Banking & Payments, Practice Management
description: The FRS 102 lease accounting changes take effect 1 January 2026 - that's your clients' next financial year-end for most. Operating leases move onto the balance sheet, impacting financial metrics and bank covenants. Are you and your clients ready? This session equips you to implement these changes efficiently: identifying affected leases, leveraging exemptions to reduce workload, performing transition calculations, and managing client concerns about sudden balance sheet impacts. What makes this stand out: practical strategies from someone who's implemented standards in small and medium practices.

title: A post-implementation review of MTD ITSA and top tips: Phase 2 and beyond
categories: Tax / VAT / MTD, Tax & MTD, Document Management
description: With the April 2026 MTD for ITSA deadline mandating those earning over £50,000 to maintain digital records and submit quarterly updates to HMRC now in effect, the UK tax landscape has fundamentally shifted from annual filings to real-time digital compliance. What have we learned? Join our expert session with Diane Wright as we review the initial rollout's successes and hurdles, while looking ahead to the next critical milestones for landlords and sole traders.

title: Ethical tax planning in practice: Balancing client pressure, risk and reputation
description: You know you need to be ethical. While the PCRT (Professional Conduct in Relation to Taxation) and HMRC's Standard for Agents set clear expectations, the most difficult decisions arise in grey areas, where commercial demands, risk and reputation collide. This session examines the real tipping points where ethical boundaries are tested in practice. Through practical scenarios, you'll gain clarity on where planning crosses the line, how to manage difficult client conversations, and how to protect your firm by building a reputation grounded in trust, integrity and sound professional judgement.

We'll explore the three pressures that most often prompt CFOs to seek peer support: increasing complexity, limited capacity, and the growing consequences of each decision. We'll also talk through the early signs that the role may have expanded beyond what one person can realistically take on, along with practical ways to assess whether additional support could improve outcomes, reduce risk, and help prevent burnout. Throughout the session, you'll hear directly from experienced CFOs who'll share their own perspectives on these challenges and how they've helped organisations navigate them.

title: From Receipt to Return: What Breaks When Annual Becomes Quarterly

description: MTD isn't a software upgrade — it's a clock speed change. Moving from annual to quarterly compliance puts pressure on every stage of your practice: onboarding, data collection, workflows, review, submission, and data security. This session maps the full lifecycle — from receipt capture to HMRC submission — highlighting where bottlenecks and capacity issues will arise. You'll leave with a clear readiness assessment and a practical onboarding timeline, so you're prepared well ahead of the first quarterly deadline.

title: CPD on steroids: The career-boosting power of volunteering

Hear real stories from finance leaders at different stages of their careers and how skills-based volunteering provides experiential learning you cannot get in a classroom. Whether you're an individual or lead a team, learn how volunteering can accelerate development while helping charities thrive.

title: The gender pensions gap: The hidden retirement crisis for women in the UK
categories: Auto Enrolment / Pensions, Payroll, HR & People
description: A girl needs to start saving for her pension at age 3. Not because she's behind — but because the system is. Our latest research shows that to retire with the same pension as a man, a woman has to start decades earlier. The gender pensions gap isn't a retirement problem. It's baked into pay, work and care from the very start of life. Drawing on now: pensions' 2024 Gender Pensions Gap report, this session pulls apart how inequality compounds over time — and asks the uncomfortable question: why are we still accepting it?

title: Why accountants need to put Bitcoin on their balance sheets
How to Win £1,000,000 in New Business (Without Chasing Anyone)
description: I'm going to literally and figuratively put money in your pocket. This session is for accountants done with guesswork, winging it, or waiting on referrals. We'll break down how to create the right environment for prospects to want to buy from you, using the R.E.P.R.E.S.E.N.T. framework: Reach: Show up in the right places Engage: Creating meaningful conversations Position: Become the clear first choice Relevance: Say what genuinely matters Environment: Let your digital presence work Strategy: Turn interest into action Evidence: Prove trust with real results Nurture: Stay front of mind Target: Attract ideal clients

Practical ways to identify weaknesses in existing AML processes and strengthen defences. What to expect next in the evolving AML landscape.

title: Planning your exit: Strategies for a smooth transition from practice ownership
description: Every practice owner will exit someday—whether by choice or circumstance. The question is: will it be on your terms? In this session, our expert panel will explore the key considerations for planning your exit, what you need to think about, and how to prepare effectively. We'll cover: • When to start planning your exit • Who and what should be factored into your planning • The different exit routes available • What third party buyers typically look for • How to prepare your practice for a successful transition • What "good" looks like in a well executed exit strategy
